task.description:
Implement the APPROVED design at src/design/iss0169-lua08-09-10-limiter-wiring.md (final version, commit 5e2b752, PASSed re-validation at commit 2afdfa1) for LUA-08 (instruction limit), LUA-09 (memory limit), LUA-10 (wall-clock timeout, including the host-external watchdog added in the design's section 2.5).

KNOWN SIGNATURE CORRECTION (flagged by CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR as CDV-0169-5, MINOR, non-blocking -- fix it during implementation, no further design cycle needed): the design's illustrative watchdog code cites `std.Thread.sleep` for the poll loop. This repo's actual Zig 0.16.0 stdlib does NOT have `std.Thread.sleep` (confirmed via `zig env` -> lib_dir -> grep Thread.zig/time.zig) -- `std.time.sleep` was also removed. The only sleep left is `std.Io.sleep`, which takes a different calling convention (requires threading an `Io` capability parameter). Find the correct Zig 0.16 primitive for a plain OS-thread sleep in a `std.Thread.spawn`-created thread that has no `Io` instance available (check how other parts of this codebase already solved a similar problem -- e.g. search for existing std.Thread usage or a low-level wait/sleep primitive already in use elsewhere in src/). This is exactly the kind of 'implementation-detail correction within this design's intent, not a design gap' the design's own section 11 anticipates -- fix it directly, do not send back to CODE-DESIGNER.

Sections to implement:
- Section 1: registry-based RunLimiter storage (replaces the lua_setglobal('__limiter__') global in instruction_limiter.zig)
- Section 2 (2.1-2.4): combined instruction-count + elapsed-time hook
- Section 2.5: host-external watchdog (WatchdogState/WatchdogHandle in timeout.zig; ExecutionContext gains active_watchdog field; call_service.zig gets pre/post activeWatchdogFired checks)
- Section 3: wiring into createSandboxedState/executeSource, including RunLimits and UNMANIFESTED_DEFAULT_LIMITS
- Section 4: memory-limiter wiring into lua_newstate
- Section 5: all five test specs (5.1 TC-LUA-08-01, 5.2 TC-LUA-09-01, 5.3 TC-LUA-10-01, 5.4 TC-LUA-10-02/spec-TC-LUA-10-03, 5.5 TC-LUA-10-03/spec-TC-LUA-10-04) -- each MUST be written so it is genuinely mutation-checkable per its own 'Mutation check' paragraph. Do not skip the mutation-check discipline -- this run's own history (see design section 11) shows tests that merely call a function without proving real enforcement have repeatedly hidden defects in this codebase (ISS-0172/GH-500 precedent).

Follow every invariant in section 9 (INV-1 through INV-4) and the design's explicit scope boundary in section 8 -- do not touch host_api/ files other than call_service.zig's pre/post watchdog checks, do not touch service_catalog.zig, events.zig, structured_logger.zig, or manifest.zig's validation logic. If implementation reveals the design cannot be followed as written for a reason beyond a small signature correction, STOP and escalate to ORCH rather than silently deviating.
acceptance_criteria: installHook uses LUA_REGISTRYINDEX, not a script-writable global
LUA-08 and LUA-10 tight-loop share one combined lua_sethook callback
LUA-10 host-external watchdog implemented per design section 2.5, using a Zig-0.16-correct sleep primitive
MemoryLimiter.alloc wired into lua_newstate via createSandboxedState
All 5 test specs (5.1-5.5) implemented and genuinely mutation-checkable
zig build, zig build test, zig build migrate all exit 0
python3 tools/lint_sql_param_types.py src tests exits 0 (if any SQL touched -- likely N/A for this pure-Zig change)
No scope creep into LUA-11/12/13/15/16 or host_api/ files beyond call_service.zig pre/post checks
Self-review checklist from CLAUDE.md BACKEND-DEV section fully passed
